run.note: This digest includes the connection-retry fix. It is not a controlled pair with the itsdangerous run, whose digest was 3714cfa6a5e81525d306f823fa3e762e6b7b385f2a375e0f599574b4a5a3f034.
run.batchExit: one arm passed, one arm failed

attempts.diagnostic: empty Memory index; parent-routed explicit evidence

falseHolds.cause: privacy preflight refusal, not a semantic hold

constraintExecution.on: not reached (harness proposal, runner probe error)

cost.note: no Jev spend because both reviews were refused before any request

findings.statement: The Jev privacy preflight refused both the Memory and the Harness review with reason sensitive and zero requests, because the assigned-credential pattern matched a placeholder credential inside a toolResult from the project's own source.
evidence: The dossier entry 6 is a toolResult; the shortest failing slice is 28 characters long and matches the assigned-credential pattern.
The masked slice reads as a passwd-style placeholder assignment of exactly the minimum length the pattern accepts.
Both reviews recorded reason sensitive with requestCount absent and durationMs 0, so no request left the process.
The off arm passed all 12 checks in the same project.
findings.impact: On any project whose tracked source, docs, or tests contain a placeholder credential assignment of eight or more characters, Jev is skipped entirely and both Memory and Harness learning are lost.
findings.decisionNeeded: Whether the preflight should treat credential-shaped placeholders inside tracked project source as sensitive. Narrowing a privacy guard changes privacy behaviour, so this needs an explicit product decision; it was not changed here.

findings.statement: The Harness effect probe aborted with FileNotFoundError after the Harness rule was rejected by parent validation.
evidence: phaseObservations.harness errorType FileNotFoundError with failedCheck phase-callback-error.
The Harness attempt sequence is rejected (parent validation, fixtures=2) then proposed (Jev propose: sensitive).
findings.impact: The probe cannot observe enforcement when no Harness rule is applied, so the arm reports a probe error instead of a clean not-applied result. This is a runner-side defect, separate from the Jev refusal.

findings.statement: The connection-retry fix has still not been exercised by a real run: no connection-level failure occurred, and the second untuned project issued zero Jev requests.
evidence: No jevJudgments entry recorded failureKind or retriedRequests in this run.
findings.impact: The fix remains proven only by its controlled tests, not by live evidence.

findings.statement: The first version of the refined gate label reported this refusal as 'unavailable or incomplete', which conflated a privacy refusal with an availability failure.
evidence: The refined helper now returns 'Jev memory review was refused by a preflight guard' for the arm's recorded receipts.
findings.status: fixed, verified against the arm's own receipts and by controlled tests

limitations: One project per protocol, and the two projects are not a controlled pair because only the second ran with the retry fix.
Two untuned projects both ended with Jev losing Memory; neither run reached a Jev semantic judgment on a supported Memory candidate.
Net benefit remains unproven, so composed and independent stay default-off in production and the goal stays open.
The cost figures for this project are incomplete because no Jev request was issued and the main-model receipt usage flags remain false.
